newsitem.title: USA: ServiceMaster notes cut by Duff & Phelps.
newsitem.headline: ServiceMaster notes cut by Duff & Phelps.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it downgraded the rating on ServiceMaster LP's senior notes to triple-B-plus from single-A-minus.
The credit rating agency also removed ServiceMaster from its watch list of companies for possible downgrades.

The downgrade was due to increased leverage stemming from recent deals at ServiceMaster. The company bought WMX Technologies Inc's 19 percent ownership interest in ServiceMaster for about $626 million in cash in April. Duff & Phelps said the transaction was financed entirely with bank debt.

ServiceMaster also acquired Barefoot Inc. for about $232 million in cash and stock in Feburary, the rating agency said. ServiceMaster expects about 50 percent of the Barefoot and WMX transactions to be ultimately refinanced through equity issuances in early 1998.

"Adjusting year-end 1996 results for the effects of the Barefoot and WMX transactions, total adjusted debt-to- capitalization increases to approximately 72 percent and fixed-charge coverage decreases to approximately 3.1 times, from actual credit protection measures of 42 percent and 5.2 times, respectively," Duff & Phelps said.

"Our rating action not only reflects the increased leverage from the Barefoot and WMX transactions, but also the expectation that ServiceMaster will continue to pursue its dividend policy and share repurchase program," Duff & Phelps said. "Our rating recognizes the company's market leading positions, outstanding free cash flow generation, which was approximately $300 million in fiscal 1996, and considerable financial flexibility."
